subject: Silvershore: targeted log retention & proof-of-delete API inquiry
messages:
From: Tom Chen <tom.chen@silvershore.dev>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant-specific log hold / selective retention capability

Hi Marissa,

Quick intro — I own security operations at Silvershore. We're running a customer-facing platform that requires us to retain certain tenant activity logs for 180 days for a compliance program in EMEA and some customers require proof-of-delete for specific cases. Our legal and procurement teams asked me to validate whether Redwood can: (1) implement a tenant-scoped retention override (keep logs for Silvershore-tenant for 180d while others remain at default 30d), (2) provide a verifiable proof-of-delete artifact when we request deletion for subsets of data, and (3) surface CAIQ/SIG evidence that specifically calls out the selective-deletion API and retention carveouts.

Questions:
- Is the selective retention per-tenant possible in hosted Redwood today, or would we need Dedicated/Private?
- What form does "proof-of-delete" take (signed manifest, hash, timestamped audit)? Can you provide a sample output?
- Are backups/replication copies covered by the same delete timelines (and how do you attest to that)?

We need this to satisfy a procurement checklist and an internal audit. If you can share a short sample artifact and a mapping to CAIQ/SIG controls that reference the selective-deletion workflow, that would be very helpful.

Happy to set a 30-minute call this week if easier.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Chen
Head of Security Operations, Silvershore

Subject: Re: Tenant-specific log hold / selective retention capability

Tom — thanks for the clear summary and for the attachment. Looping in Ben (Security Eng) and Kimberly (Compliance) so we can answer both the technical and attestation pieces.

Short answers up front:
- We can support tenant-scoped retention overrides in hosted Redwood for some log classes (session traces, request-level debug logs) via tenant tags and TTL-exempt rules; there are operational caveats for retention of backups and long-term archives.
- Proof-of-delete: we produce a signed deletion manifest (JSON) that includes deleted object ids, deletion job id, timestamp, and a SHA256 hash bundle signed by our KMS-backed signing key. We can provide a sample artifact.
- CAIQ/SIG evidence: we have a packaged excerpt that maps the deletion workflow to relevant SIG controls and lists required evidence artifacts.

Ben/Kim — please see Tom's ask below. To scope the work we need: 1) a clear list of log categories you want kept 180d, 2) whether you need index/searchability preserved (we can keep raw blobs but remove indexing), and 3) confirmation on legal POV (is this an ongoing contractual requirement or a timebound audit?).

Tom — can you do a 30-min sync on Wed Dec 1, 10:30am PT? Ben and Kimberly can join. We'll bring a short tech runbook and an evidence packet.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Tom / team — following up with the technical detail we discussed. Attaching two artifacts: redwood-sig-caiq-excerpt.pdf (high-level mapping for SIG/CAIQ items we commonly surface) and sample-proof-of-delete-log.txt (a redacted example of a signed deletion manifest).

Summary of technical approach (high level):
- Tenant tagging: logs are labeled with tenant_id at ingest. Retention policies evaluate tenant_id + log_class to decide TTL. We support per-tenant TTL overrides for 'session-trace', 'request-debug', and 'audit-event' classes in hosted mode when the request rate and storage profile are within thresholds.
- Proof-of-delete: deletion is a two-phase job — (1) logical deletion (remove index entries, mark objects for purge), (2) physical purge job that deletes objects and writes a signed manifest: {job_id, tenant_id, object_ids[], deletion_epoch, sha256_bundle, signer_key_id}. The manifest is signed by our HSM-backed key and stored immutably for 7 years for audit. The sample file shows format and a fake signature stub.
- Backups & replication: active deletion triggers the same purge pipeline for primary copies; however, cold backups and remote archive replicas may have separate retention windows. For customers requiring unconditional purge across all copies, we recommend Dedicated or Private with an agreed restore-window/backup policy and contractually defined backup purge timelines.

Caveats and next steps:
- For hosted carveouts we require an SOW and an operational review (storage impact, snapshot window) before enabling on production.
- We will need a legal/PO artifact for any long-tail retention override; this is standard for SLA/contract exceptions.

Proposed deliverables before your procurement deadline:
1) One-page evidence summary (controls mapping + explanation)
2) Sample signed deletion manifest (attached)
3) Proposed SOW language for retention carveout

Available slots for the workshop: Wed Dec 1 10:30am PT (confirmed) or Thu Dec 2 9:00am PT.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
